hyps.why: Filling an empty direct input-to-output edge with a 3x3 conv adds a whole path, whereas replacing an existing op gives a smaller gain.
Adding a skip where the edge was removed helps gradient flow, whereas replacing a conv with a skip loses accuracy.
Edge 4 only receives input through edge 0, so it is dead when edge 0 is none and the edit has little effect.
Edge 2 is fed only by node 1, which is disconnected from the input when edge 0 is none.
Removing a 3x3 conv on an output edge costs far more than removing a weak op such as avg pool or none.
With edge 1 removed, edge 5 can only be reached via 0->1->2, so a conv on it contributes less.
Diminishing returns: another strong conv path to the output adds less when one already exists.
Replacing a conv with pooling loses much more accuracy than replacing a weak op.
With edge 4 removed, edge 0 contributes only via 0->1->2->3, so a conv on it gives less benefit.
Edge 1 feeds node 2, whose only exit is edge 5, so a conv on it is wasted when edge 5 is none.
